guide.summary: Custom OAuth app, unpublished, customer admins (approval path unconfirmed); Listed in Box Integrations (published) (app review). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Box. The separate Box MCP toolkit (BOX_MCP) requires your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Box app. For launch you likely want your own app so consent shows your brand and you get dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
Composio's default scopes may not cover what you need

scenarios.label: Custom OAuth app, unpublished, customer admins
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent uses a user-authentication OAuth 2.0 app that is not listed in Box Integrations; customers connect with their own Box accounts.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No timeline found for customer admin approval; Box docs give no review wait for unpublished apps.

scenarios.approval: No Box review is described for unpublished OAuth apps. A customer's Box Admin may need to enable the app, depending on their settings.

scenarios.label: Listed in Box Integrations (published)
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want your OAuth app listed in the Box Integrations directory to reach other enterprises.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count; checklist and assets are on a page not in the dossier

scenarios.approval: Submission for approval in the Developer Console, followed by a partner review process that the docs do not describe.
gate_sequence: Fill out submission form in Developer Console

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account gives access to the Developer Console. Not every product is included on the free plan.

prerequisites.title: Production-ready OAuth 2.0 app for listing
prerequisites.detail: Listing in Box Integrations requires a production-ready app that uses OAuth 2.0.

steps.title: Create User-type app in Developer Console
steps.detail: Log in, select New App, choose User as the app type, and create it.
steps.done_when: The app exists with a Client ID and secret.

steps.title: Get redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard for the Box auth config.

steps.title: Configure scopes and redirect URI
steps.detail: Set scopes and add the redirect URI on the Configuration tab. The URI must match exactly and use HTTPS.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config via API
steps.detail: Create the Box auth config in Composio with your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Ask customer admins to enable the app
steps.detail: Give the customer's Box Admin your Client ID so they can enable the app in the Admin Console if required.

steps.title: Submit app for Box Integrations approval
steps.detail: Fill out the form in the Developer Console and select Submit.

steps.title: Wait for Box partner review
steps.detail: Box reviews the submission; timing is not documented.

traps.title: Box's general API limit is 1000 API requests per
traps.detail: Box's general API limit is 1000 API requests per minute per user. The page does not say whether this applies differently to unreviewed apps.

traps.title: Box's upload limit is 240 file upload requests per
traps.detail: Box's upload limit is 240 file upload requests per minute per user. The page does not say whether this applies differently to unreviewed apps.

traps.title: Scope changes need re-authorization
traps.detail: When scopes or access level change, the app must be re-authorized; enterprise developers resubmit to their Box Admin.

traps.title: App type cannot be changed
traps.detail: An OAuth 2.0 app cannot be changed to Server Authentication later. You must create a new app.

traps.title: Multiple redirect URIs need a redirect_uri parameter
traps.detail: If several are configured and the parameter is missing, users see a redirect_uri_missing error.

traps.title: Tokens expire
traps.detail: Access tokens last 60 minutes; refresh tokens last 60 days or one use.

traps.title: API calls count toward customer allocation
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward the customer's monthly allocation, including authentication requests; partner integrations do not.

blockers.symptom: Users cannot use the app because their enterprise has unpublished apps disabled
blockers.what_it_means: The customer's Box Admin turned on 'Disable unpublished apps by default', so an Admin must enable any OAuth 2.0 app.
blockers.what_to_do: Send the Admin your Client ID and ask them to enable the app in the Admin Console.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request email for the customer admin.

blockers.what_it_means: The redirect URI is missing or does not exactly match a configured one.
blockers.what_to_do: Check that the redirect_uri parameter matches a configured URI exactly.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the configured and requested URIs.

open_questions: How long does Box's partner review for Box Integrations listing take? Ask Box partner support or read the Box Integrations page.
What does the partner review check? The docs do not describe it; read the Box Integrations submission checklist.
Do any usage limits apply to unreviewed apps? The rate-limit page does not say; ask Box developer support.
Which scopes does Composio's managed Box app request? Check the Composio Box toolkit page.

The quote says to publish, the app must be production-ready and use OAuth 2.0.
The quote points to Box Integrations for the partner review process and gives no description of it, which matches the statement.
The quote instructs the developer to fill out the form and select Submit.
The quote says a Box Admin or Co-Admin needs an application's Client ID to authorize or enable it. The truncation falls after 'authorize or', so the cut-off words are the only gap.

The quote says enterprise developers must submit the app for re-authorization by the Box Admin after saving changes.
The quote says access tokens are valid for 60 minutes but can be revoked, which matches the statement's 'unless revoked earlier'.
The quote states refresh tokens are valid for 60 days or one use.
The quote says the enterprise's monthly allocation includes authentication requests. It does not list custom applications, scripts, or integrations as counting toward it.
The quote says Box partner integrations and native Box applications don't count toward the allocation.

The quotes support the admin enablement step, but say nothing about creating the app in the Developer Console or configuring scopes and the redirect URI.
The quotes say admins decide whether unpublished apps are enabled by default and describe the 'Disable unpublished apps by default' setting, which matches the statement.
The quotes say publishing requires submitting the app for approval and point to a partner review process, so the provider reviews the app before it is listed.
The quotes say publishing requires submission for approval and reference a partner review process. They do not say the review is always required in every case.
